deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Euler's table of 'divisores ipsius aa+1' for a = 580 to 637. It serves the aim of E283: finding very large primes of the form a²+1, and in general identifying primes through quadratic forms.

How the table is built (a sieve): a prime p divides a²+1 exactly when p = 2 or p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and a ≡ ±r (mod p), where r² ≡ −1. So each such p strikes out two residue classes of a.

What each entry records: only the prime factors smaller than a, with exponents. A product of two factors each larger than a would exceed a²+1, so at most one prime factor of a²+1 exceeds a. Hence the unlisted cofactor is always 1 or a single prime.
- A blank entry for even a means a²+1 is prime. The blanks here are 584, 594, 634 and 636, which agree with the known list of n with n²+1 prime (OEIS A005574).
- An entry of '2' alone for odd a means (a²+1)/2 is prime.

Spot checks:
- 580² + 1 = 336401 = 13·113·229
- 583² + 1 = 2·5·41·829 (829 > a, so omitted)
- 593² + 1 = 2·5²·13·541
- 599² + 1 = 2·17·61·173
- 601² + 1 = 2·313·577
- 606² + 1 = 13²·41·53
- 612² + 1 = 5·173·433
- 616² + 1 = 13·17²·101
- 621² + 1 = 2·29·61·109
- 582² + 1 = 5²·17·797 (797 omitted)
- 585² + 1 = 2·137·1249
- 610² + 1 = 233·1597
- 624² + 1 = 41·9497 (9497 is prime)

All are consistent with the rule 'list primes below a'.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the entries checked on this page.
At 621 the factor 29 is printed out of order (2. 61. 109. 29), apparently a late insertion; the factorization itself is correct.
At 593 there is a stray period after 541.

ideas.what: Sieve for prime divisors of a²+1 using the two square roots of −1 mod p, giving a table of small factors and a test for primality of a²+1.
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic-polynomial sieve; tables of factors of n²+1 (later Cunningham, 'Quadratic partitions' and n²+1 factor tables)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E283) for the early table; extended by Cunningham and others in the 19th–20th centuries

ideas.what: Observation that a²+1 has at most one prime factor exceeding a, so listing the factors below a determines the full factorization.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary bound on large prime factors of n²+1
ideas.where_published: E283 (implicit in the construction of the table)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct computational table belonging to a well-known Euler paper whose method and results are documented; there are no new ideas on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'Diuifores ipfius' is the long-s rendering of 'Diuisores ipsius'.
Next-page note: at 693 the entry '2 5^3. 12. 113' should read '2. 5^3. 17. 113', since 693²+1 = 480250 = 2·5³·17·113.
